name: Camilism
summary: Camilism is the revolutionary Christian thought of the Colombian priest and sociologist Camilo Torres Restrepo, built on 'effective love': love of neighbour must be made effective, which requires taking power from the privileged minority for the poor majority, by peaceful means if they do not resist and by force if they do. His 1965 United Front programme joins land reform without compensation, State ownership of banks, resources and health care, compulsory planning and progressive taxation with political pluralism, cooperation with communists on common goals and a refusal to join the Communist Party.
scope: Torres's own political writings and speeches of 1962-1966, above all the 1965 United Front platforms (the Medellin and Bogota versions), his Messages in the Frente Unido newspaper, the 1963 lecture on democracy, and the 1965 essay on the Christian imperative to revolution, read with Herrera Farfan's scholarly study of effective love. It does not cover later guerrilla conduct of the ELN, other liberation theologies or Marxism-Leninism generally, and no regime applied it, so there is no record beyond Torres's own words. His 1966 turn to the armed road was brief, so his peaceful-or-forced stance of 1965 counts as the mature one.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The platform keeps armed forces and he held there will be an army to defend the people while reaction endures.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Banks are to be State-owned, foreign-currency operations exclusively the State's, and the money supply planned.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The platform makes land the property of those who work it directly.

arms-reduction.rationale: The platform sets the military budget to the mission without hurting health and education, and Medellin cuts it to a minimum.

bound-labor.rationale: The platform gives land to the person who works it directly and expropriates estates, which excludes land bound to a lord.

capital-controls.rationale: Foreign-currency operations belong to the State alone, and he said capital export must be prohibited to keep investment at home.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Banks are to be State-owned and foreign-exchange dealings the State's alone, leaving no room for an independent central bank.

central-planning.rationale: Torres held that an effective plan requires the State to steer investment coercively, citing Soviet planning as the case where State control let a poor country develop.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: He held that charity and alms cannot feed, clothe and teach the majority, so structural means are needed.

class-collaboration.rationale: He called for the union of the oppressed against the oppressors and for taking power from the privileged minority, not for cooperation with the employing class.

clerical-rule.rationale: He wanted the Church stripped of political interference and power to rest with organised majorities.

collective-farming.rationale: The land reform asks that exploitation be by cooperative and communal systems under a national agrarian plan, with title going to those who work the land.

communal-electorates.rationale: He wanted political unity above religions, which separate religious electorates would cut across.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He cited Aquinas that the people make the concrete attribution of authority and that authority against the people is illegitimate and called tyranny.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: He criticised the oligarchy's luxury spending and the bourgeois purchase of prestige symbols.

corporate-influence.rationale: He held that an economic minority and foreign interests make the country's basic decisions.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: He denounced sales and fuel taxes as burdens loaded on the people.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The programme builds an integral and progressive social-security scheme covering unemployment, disability, old age and death.

decide-locally.rationale: The programme builds popular power from the village and neighbourhood up and revives elected municipalities, yet also imposes a compulsory national plan on all investment.

defeat-communism.rationale: He said he was not anti-communist as a Colombian, sociologist, Christian or priest and would fight alongside communists for common goals.

delink-world-market.rationale: The platform calls for relations and trade with every country on terms of equity and mutual benefit.

democracy-becomes-oligarchy.rationale: He held that the industrial democracies are genuine because organised majorities control power, though liberal and socialist forms have each turned oligarchic.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He said democracy is not a legal formula but a relation of forces, and that orderly elections run by a minority give oligarchy.

direct-action.rationale: He rejected the electoral route for active abstention and organisation from below, and later the armed road, but said a peaceful handover would be taken peacefully.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The platform has women take part on equal footing with men in economic, political and social life.

dominated-front.rationale: He called for uniting the weak and oppressed countries against exploitation and said Latin Americans must unite with the enemies of the United States.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He condemned the keeping of a state of siege and detention without warrant or intercepted mail as violations of the constitution.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: His neutralism rejects falling into either bloc, though he names no treaty.

equal-conscription.rationale: Medellin has all Colombians, men and women, serve two years of civic service in place of military service.

experts-over-public.rationale: The platform wants technical planning but says the aim is that organised majorities themselves produce the decisions.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The tax plank is a progressive tax on larger incomes.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: Health care and education are to be free to all Colombians.

free-public-college.rationale: The State gives education free to all Colombians, respecting the student's own ideology after secondary school.

free-trade.rationale: The programme restricts imports to capital goods that serve national development and plans import substitution.

gradual-change.rationale: He demanded fast, fundamental change and called reformist legislation a distraction from structural change.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The platform holds that independence demands decisions that hit the interests of the economic minority, and he noted independence from Spain led only to dependence on the United States.

independent-unions.rationale: He praised unions as independent, condemned leaders bought by government and the Medellin programme guarantees union freedom and pluralism.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The platform puts indigenous councils in real possession of the lands that belong to them and promises to strengthen indigenous communities.

informal-organisation.rationale: His commands of five or ten were to federate into municipal, regional and national commands under a national convention, not stay informal.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He urged poor countries to seek their own route after finding that liberal and socialist democracy both turned oligarchic.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: He condemned the American landing in Santo Domingo and the war in Vietnam as crimes.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: Medellin counts votes in assemblies by persons and not by capital and gives workers equality with capital in running firms.

land-redistribution.rationale: The land is owned by the person who works it directly, estates are expropriated without compensation and title goes to peasants.

leader-cult.rationale: The programme avoids personalism and caudillismo, and he asked that the platform not be tied to his name.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Hospitals and clinics are State-owned and public transport State or cooperative-run, with water a natural resource.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Torres argued that without the State directing investment by compulsory plan no efficiency in favour of the majority is possible, and the programme abolishes free enterprise.

maximum-personal-income.rationale: Income above a decorous family level passes entirely to the State unless invested as the plan directs.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The platform makes hospitals, clinics and drug supply State-owned and health staff government employees, though private practice is not barred.

national-church-status.rationale: He wanted the Concordat revised to remove the Church's privileges and political role.

national-resource-control.rationale: Subsoil ownership belongs to the State, and foreign oil concessions are allowed only on strict conditions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He called on poor countries to look for their own route after finding that liberal and socialist democracy both fell into oligarchy.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: He said it is the duty of revolutionaries not to let themselves be killed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The programme gives the State planning, nationalised sectors, free health and education.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: He said the programme must unite across religions and ideologies and enter no religious ground.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: He rejected occasional, paternalistic charity and held the privileged will not choose effective means since these cost their privileges.

one-party-rule.rationale: The programme calls for a pluralist political apparatus that respects each group's ideology, and Torres warned that socialist democracy too can turn into oligarchy.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: He declared the legal routes exhausted and the armed route the only one left.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: He argued that opposition in parliament cannot make revolutionary changes and only lends the oligarchy a democratic cover.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The programme builds planning on community action and gives workers a say in company direction and profits.

party-controls-media.rationale: Medellin keeps the press, radio, TV and film free but subject to State control for the common good, and radio and TV are State-owned in the platform.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: He described women as placed in inferiority to men and society in every class, with the law's equality not real.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: He called on every patriotic Colombian to join a struggle for a homeland independent of United States power and for the popular class.

people-in-arms.rationale: The platform puts defence of sovereignty in the hands of the whole people, yet he keeps an army for the people's defence while the enemy lasts.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The platform and his speeches describe the ruling minority as deciding for its own interests, and he called the political system disintegrated and corrupt.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He argued that investment planning must be supranational through regional integration, and the programme ties trade policy to Latin American integration.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He held that lack of solutions is not the problem; poverty continues because those holding power refuse to apply them.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: He said the great press serves the oligarchy and deforms popular movements, so the people need their own organ.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Effective love, the core of his thought, means seeking effective means for the well-being of the majority who go unfed, unclothed and untaught.

production-for-use.rationale: The programme replaces free enterprise by cooperative enterprise, puts investment under a plan serving the majority and makes usury, hoarding and speculation crimes.

property-franchise.rationale: A franchise by property would shut out the poor majority whose decisions he demanded.

property-fundamental.rationale: The platform expropriates land without compensation where the common good requires it and gives title to those who work it, so private property is not an overriding right.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Land needed for the common good is expropriated, and he said property must be organised so that society is never sacrificed to individuals.

public-money-creation.rationale: Banks are State-owned and the Medellin programme issues money only to expand production.

public-ownership.rationale: The platform places banks, insurance, hospitals, public transport, radio and television and natural resources in State hands, with oil exploited by the State.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Torres was a Catholic priest who held that the Church is divine and that effective love joins faith with science, so reason is not the only guide.

regional-resource-ownership.rationale: The programme gives the subsoil and resources to the national State.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Every public or private investment must fit the compulsory national plan, and foreign oil concessions are tied to State share, refining and wage conditions.

religion-illusion.rationale: He held the Church to be divine and Christianity the basis of effective love, and said a Church that urged conformity would be the opium of the people.

religious-nation.rationale: His movement was to unite the popular class without religious differences.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: The platform returns real possession of land to indigenous councils.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Christians may and must fight tyranny, and he held the government to have violated the constitution.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: His slogans pledge struggle for popular power to the death and his proclamation ends with liberation or death.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: He treated legal and illegal strikes as strengthening the revolutionary struggle.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He urged analysing each country's problems objectively without philosophical or ideological prejudice, and the movement unites on concrete technical objectives.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Authority rests on the people, and the movement is to be built around principles and not a leader.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He called aid crumbs and warned foreign investment brings dependence, yet allowed foreign oil concessions on conditions and welcomed technical aid.

separate-church-state.rationale: He wanted the Concordat reformed so the Church loses political interference and a State autonomous of the hierarchy, though not a hostile separation.

social-market-economy.rationale: The programme abolishes free enterprise for planning and cooperatives, which departs from a market economy with a social net.

socialism-needs-revolutionary-war.rationale: He said power could be taken peacefully if handed over, and in January 1966 said only the armed road remained.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He charged the government with violating the constitution and the law and called for a regime where the people decide.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: He told supporters to collect arms and organise armed commands of the Front.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He says the ruling minority makes the State's decisions in countries like Colombia, yet that organised majorities control the State in the industrial democracies.

state-directs-investment.rationale: All investment, public or private, must follow the national investment plan and surplus income goes to the State unless invested as the plan directs.

state-finances-worker-businesses.rationale: The programme backs cooperatives by every means with credit and technical help.

state-harmful.rationale: The programme builds a planning State that owns the banks, resources and health service, which a doctrine of the State as harmful could not accept.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He said he would not proselytise communists, and held that Christians can build socialism if allowed to worship.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He declared himself personally in favour of neutralism like Egypt, Yugoslavia and India.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He condemned persecution of the discontented as anticommunism and McCarthyism, and called for pluralism.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The programme gives health care and education free to all rather than to the poorest alone.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The programme plans import substitution and allows only imports that serve national development, which protects domestic industry, though it names no tariffs.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The tax plank charges a progressive tax on income above a decorous family level and passes any surplus not invested under the plan to the State.

taxation-theft.rationale: The tax plank is a steeply progressive tax on high incomes.

total-state.rationale: The State plans the economy, yet education respects parents' and then students' ideology and religion is kept outside the programme.

trade-surplus.rationale: The planning plank aims to substitute imports and raise exports.

unions-good.rationale: He treats unions and strikes as building revolutionary consciousness and wants workers organised in unions to share in running firms, while condemning government-bought leaders.

unions-run-economy.rationale: The economy is run under a State plan, with unions taking part in company management.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The platform commits the State to a comprehensive social-security plan that guarantees health and medical care free to the population.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: He used Aquinas that authority against the people is illegitimate tyranny that Christians may fight, which bears on unjust rule.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Legitimacy rests on the people, and the platform stays out of religious ground.

vanguard-party.rationale: He called for disciplined, firm organisation and had Front militants lead, yet insisted on a movement from the base without caudillos and had workers decide the moment.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He argued that liberal democracy turned oligarchic through ownership of the means of production.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The programme gives land to those who work it and makes urban residents owners of their homes, but also nationalises major sectors and prefers cooperative farming.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: He gave up the duties of the clergy to join the revolution, and held passive faith is not enough.

women-distinct-values.rationale: He praised women's generosity, sensitivity and intuition as qualities to be exalted in the revolution.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: He said women's equality of rights would become real only after an authentic revolution.

women-suffrage.rationale: The programme gives women equal standing in the political activities of the country.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: He wanted a network sustaining the organisation of the working and peasant class and the unity of workers with the peasantry.

worker-ownership.rationale: The Medellin programme replaces free enterprise with cooperative and community enterprise and lets workers hold shares and take part in direction and profits.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: He accepted any patriotic Colombian, including progressive bourgeois individuals, but found few nationalist capitalists.

workers-own-party.rationale: He sought a political apparatus capable of taking power, independent of the traditional parties.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: He said reformist pressure leaves structures intact and labour law served as a distraction.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Medellin counts votes in company assemblies by persons rather than shares and lets workers take part equally in direction, administration and profits.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: He said the United States wants cheap raw materials and sells dear manufactures, keeping Colombia dependent.

missingStatements.text: Opposition movements should boycott elections that a ruling elite controls.
missingStatements.rationale: Torres practised and argued active abstention in 1965 because the electoral machinery is controlled by the oligarchy and opposition in parliament only lends it a democratic cover.

quotes.text: Personalmente yo soy partidario de la abstención electoral pero no de una abstención pasiva, sino de una abstención activa, beligerante y revolucionaria.
quotes.where: Camilo Torres, archivochile text ct0029 (see source s6)

quotes.text: La abstención electoral, por sí sola, no es un arma de combate revolucionaria; ella tiene que estar acompañada de una organización y de una disciplina beligerante y activa.
quotes.where: Camilo Torres, archivochile text ct0027 (see source s17)

quotes.text: nosotros no podemos ir a hacerle el juego a las oligarquías metiéndonos en su sistema electoral, controlado por ellas
quotes.where: Camilo Torres, archivochile text ct0023 (see source s16)

missingStatements.text: Opponents of a ruling elite should unite around a minimal common programme despite their ideological and religious differences.
missingStatements.rationale: The Front rests on a common platform that sets aside ideological and religious disputes, including with communists, to fight the ruling minority.

quotes.text: Tenemos nosotros que lograr la unión revolucionaria por encima de las ideologías que nos separan.
quotes.where: Camilo Torres, archivochile text ct0044 (see source s23)

quotes.text: Entonces tenemos que pasar por encima de las diferencias religiosas
quotes.where: Camilo Torres, archivochile text ct0023 (see source s16)

quotes.text: Sin embargo, estoy dispuesto a luchar con ellos por objetivos comunes: contra la oligarquía y el dominio de los Estados Unidos
quotes.where: Camilo Torres, archivochile text ct0025 (see source s3)

missingStatements.declined: A tactical choice of opposition movements, not a general position.

notes: Searched every theme in Torres's collected 1960-66 texts on archivochile (platforms, messages, interviews, lectures) and Marxists Internet Archive messages, and keyword-searched the 1985 Escritos volume (not cited). Government, economy and world themes are well covered by the platforms; liberty, culture, ecology, technology and most society themes are unaddressed and stay null (no mention of drugs, guns, abortion, same-sex marriage, climate or nuclear power was found). The platform's two versions differ (Medellin allows cooperative or State transport and sets oil conditions at 80 percent and 10 years; the later Bogota text 70 percent and 25 years); answers rest on points they share. Wikipedia's definition of Camilism as including later Montoneros or Sandinista currents was not used.

keyFigures.role: Colombian priest and sociologist who founded the United Front and whose thought gives the ideology its name
keyFigures.quote: El amor eficaz de Camilo Torres Restrepo: elementos para la discusióni Revista Kavilando Grupo de Investigación
